note: Conformance vectors for the data-point address grammar. Shared, not owned:
dossier and qmcp each implement the grammar and each run these cases, which
is how two implementations stay honest without one importing the other.
docs/ref/addresses.md is the grammar. ci/addresses.py is the reference
implementation and `uv run qm addresses --check` runs this file against it.
Every case with valid=true must parse to the declared parts AND format back
to the identical string. The round trip is the point: an address that does
not survive it cannot link a dashboard row to the thing it names.
Adding a case is cheap and is the right response to any address that was
read wrongly in the wild. Removing one needs a reason.

cases.why: a bare owner/repo denotes the repository itself
the case the grammar exists for: a namespaced branch keeps its slash, so the id is the ref git accepts. 30 of 32 branches here look like this
a legal branch name that the old slug collapsed onto the case above. Both must exist and stay distinct
an unnamespaced branch is not a special case
a propagation branch: slash and hyphens and digits together
ids stay strings; nothing here coerces a number
the tag as pushed, dots included
the kind the milestone needs: a workflow step and a delta are one unit of work, addressed once
the audit record a delta links to. A UUID has hyphens and no slashes
a kind name appearing inside an id must not re-trigger a kind match. Substring parsing gets this wrong
`tools` is not a kind, so this is not a repo-scoped address. The closed kind set is what makes an ordinary path distinguishable from an address
a kind with no id addresses nothing
an owner alone is not a data point
the empty string is swept past, not parsed
a reserved global bucket. Not repo-scoped, and listed so that an owner named `github` is a collision somebody chose
